newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPAIN'S KING: politician's death was "not in vain".
newsitem.headline: SPAIN'S KING: politician's death was "not in vain".

text.p: King Juan Carlos told the Spanish people on Monday night that the death of Miguel Angel Blanco -- a young politician killed by Basque separatists -- "has not been in vain".
In a rare televised message to the nation, the king sought to reassure Spaniards, telling them he had "followed with great emotion the condemnation of terrorism throughout Spain".
In a taped message from the lawn of the royal palace, the king praised the widespread reaction to the brutal killing of Blanco, whose body was found bound and bloodied on Saturday.
Millions of people have taken to the streets throughout the country to mourn Blanco's death and condemn the Basque separatist guerrillas.

"The Spanish have given an unsurpassable example of civility and unity. I would tell them that the death of Miguel Angel has not been in vain, and to continue fighting in this endless struggle for democracy, liberty and human rights," the king said.

Blanco, 29, was killed after ETA rebels kidnapped him and demanded the government move about 500 ETA inmates to the Basque region before 4 p.m on Saturday. He was found with two gunshot wounds in his head shortly after the deadline and died nearly 12 hours later.
More than a million people attended a demonstration led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar in central Madrid on Monday night to protest the killing.
"The conscience of the Spanish people has been displayed on the street, demonstrating how emphatically they want to continue working for democracy, human rights," the king said.
The king, who usually tries to stay clear of politics, sent his son Crown Prince Felipe to Blanco's funeral in the Basque town of Ermua on Monday. Aznar also attended the funeral.
